messages.author: b3d929c6746ca81a
messages.subject: RE: [dartR] merge
parts:
In dartR 1.5.5 (still in development so please use with care) there is a gl.join function

 

 

You need to have two dart files with exactly the same number of loci and metadata (individuals and loci).

 

Then it works simply via

 

Glnew <- gl.join(gl1, gl2)

 

gl1 and  gl2 being your two genlight objects created via your gl.read.dart() function calls.

 

Cheers, Bernd

 

See also the example via ?gl.join

messages.author: a3ea45e87285d820
messages.subject: Re: [dartR] merge
parts:
Hi Farhad,

gl.join() is designed to join two genlight objects created from the same service, such as when DArT splits the csv datafile in two because of size limitations of Excel. As such, it expects two genlight objects with the exact same individuals and individual metadata, and two different sets of loci in each genlight object.

I can see how one might want to join genlight objects with different individuals but the same loci, or different loci scored across the same individuals, but cannot see a situation where you would want to join two genlight objects with different individuals and different loci. Can you elaborate on your need?

A

messages.subject: Re: [dartR] merge
parts:
Hi Farhad,

In that case, by far the best option is to list your first service when submitting samples to DArT for a second service so that they can run both data sets through their pipelines together. This is the best option because calling the SNPs is not a locus by locus exercise, but the DArT folk examine the data manually and make decisions on thresholds based on global attributes. As an extreme case, some loci that would not make the mark when examining the first dataset may do so in the combined analysis.

You can ask DArT to combine your two services into one analysis, and maybe they will do it for no or a minimal charge?

A
